title: Geometric Hahn Banach and Convex Separation

items.title: Absorbing, balanced, and absolutely convex subsets of a normed space
items.strategy: Define absorption by positive scalar dilates, balance by scalars of modulus at most one, and absolute convexity as convex and balanced; record the real/complex scalar convention explicitly.

items.title: The Minkowski functional of an absorbing set
items.strategy: For an absorbing set C, define p_C(x)=inf{t>0:x in tC}; prove finiteness from absorption, while reserving homogeneity, subadditivity, and definiteness for subsequent results.

items.title: The gauge of an absorbing convex set is sublinear
items.strategy: Use convex combinations of scaled representatives and epsilon-approximations to the infimum to prove positive real homogeneity and the triangle inequality without assuming an infimum is attained.

items.title: The gauge of an absorbing absolutely convex set is a seminorm
items.strategy: Combine sublinearity with balance to upgrade nonnegative real homogeneity to p_C(lambda x)=|lambda|p_C(x), including the zero scalar; state the seminorm laws explicitly rather than calling the gauge a norm.

items.title: An open convex neighbourhood of zero is its gauge sublevel set
items.strategy: For an open convex set U containing zero, use openness for U={p_U<1}, and extract a norm-ball inclusion to bound p_U continuously; do not assert this equality for a translated set until it has been translated to contain zero.

items.title: Weak and strict separation by a continuous functional
items.strategy: Define the inequalities for two sets through one nonzero member of X*, using Re f in the complex case; distinguish a one-sided strict inequality from a positive uniform gap.

items.title: An open convex set and an exterior point are strictly separated
items.strategy: Choose a point of the open convex set, translate it to an open convex neighbourhood of zero, use its gauge on the line through the translated exterior point, and apply dominated Hahn--Banach; pass from a real separator to a complex-linear one by real part when required.

items.title: Disjoint convex sets, one open, are weakly separated with strictness on the open side
items.strategy: Apply point-versus-open separation to the open convex difference A-B and zero, then rewrite its single inequality as a common functional bound on A and B; retain the asymmetric strictness stated by the theorem.

items.title: A closed convex set and a disjoint compact convex set are strongly separated
items.strategy: Use continuity of distance to the closed set and compactness to obtain a positive minimum distance; thicken the closed convex set by a sufficiently small open ball and apply one-open separation to obtain a positive functional gap.

items.title: A closed convex set is the intersection of its containing closed half-spaces
items.strategy: The easy containment is immediate; for each exterior point, separate a small open ball about it from the closed convex set and retain the containing closed functional half-space that excludes the point.

items.title: The continuous annihilator of a linear subspace
items.strategy: Define M^perp={f in X*:f|_M=0}; keep this continuous-dual notation distinct from the earlier algebraic annihilator U^circ under an evaluation pairing.

items.title: A vector outside a subspace closure is detected by a normed annihilator
items.strategy: For x outside closure(M), define on M+Kx the coefficient functional m+lambda x maps to lambda, bound it exactly by dist(x,M)^{-1}, and extend norm-preservingly; state both f|_M=0, f(x)=1 and the distance-normalised form.

items.title: The closure of a subspace is the common kernel of its continuous annihilator
items.strategy: Every annihilator functional vanishes on closure(M) by continuity, while the geometric Hahn--Banach theorem supplies one that excludes every point outside closure(M).

items.title: A subspace is dense exactly when its continuous annihilator is zero
items.strategy: Specialise the closure--annihilator identity to closure(M)=X, and prove the converse by observing that a nonzero separating functional prevents density.

items.title: Every finite-dimensional subspace of a normed space is complemented
items.strategy: Extend the coordinate functionals of a fixed ordered basis by norm-preserving Hahn--Banach, assemble the resulting finite coordinate sum into a bounded projection, and invoke the published projection criterion.

items.title: Every closed finite-codimensional subspace of a normed space is complemented
items.strategy: Give X/M its published quotient norm, choose representatives of a finite quotient basis, construct a bounded linear section by finite coordinates, and subtract its quotient lift from the identity to obtain a bounded projection onto M.

items.title: A linear hyperplane as a codimension-one subspace
items.strategy: Define a linear hyperplane H of X by dim(X/H)=1, with quotient-coset notation and codimension convention made explicit.

items.title: The closed linear hyperplanes are exactly kernels of nonzero continuous functionals
items.strategy: For a closed hyperplane, use geometric Hahn--Banach on any exterior vector and the one-dimensional quotient decomposition to identify its kernel; conversely show a nonzero continuous functional has a closed codimension-one kernel.

items.title: Mazur's theorem: weak and norm closures of a convex set agree
items.strategy: State weak closure locally through finite families of X* functionals, pending the later weak-topology definition; closed functional half-spaces make norm closure weakly closed, while norm convergence satisfies the finite-functional weak condition.

title: Geometric Hahn Banach and Convex Separation — Examples

items.title: Gauges of norm balls and finite-dimensional ellipsoids
items.strategy: Compute the gauge of an open or closed norm unit ball as the norm, then compute a diagonal ellipsoid gauge in finite coordinates and identify its induced norm.

items.title: The gauge of an absorbing convex nonbalanced set need not be a seminorm
items.strategy: Use C=(-1,2) in the real line, calculate its gauge separately on positive and negative scalars, and exhibit p_C(1) not equal to p_C(-1).

items.title: Two disjoint closed convex sets need not be strongly separated
items.strategy: Use the epigraph of exp and the horizontal axis in R^2: verify closedness and convexity from continuity and two-point convexity of exp, then use distance zero along x tending to negative infinity to rule out a positive functional gap.

items.title: Distance to a subspace via norm-one annihilating functionals
items.strategy: Derive dist(x,M)=sup{|f(x)|:f in M^perp, ||f|| at most 1}, treating x in closure(M) separately and using the geometric Hahn--Banach functional for equality outside it.

items.title: The supremum-norm spaces ell-infinity and c-zero
items.strategy: Define ell-infinity as bounded scalar sequences with the supremum norm and c-zero as its subspace of sequences converging to zero; verify the elementary vector-space and norm conventions needed by the Phillips example.

items.title: c-zero is a closed subspace of ell-infinity
items.strategy: Show that a uniform limit of null sequences is null by a two-epsilon estimate, so c-zero is a closed linear subspace and its quotient carries the published quotient norm.

items.title: There is an uncountable almost-disjoint family of infinite subsets of the natural numbers
items.strategy: Fix an enumeration of the rationals and choose least-index rational approximants to each irrational, so no choice is hidden; their ranges are infinite and pairwise almost disjoint after repeated terms are removed explicitly.

items.title: Assuming countable choice, (ell-infinity/c-zero)* has no countable separating family
items.strategy: Use characteristic functions of an uncountable almost-disjoint family to show each quotient functional is nonzero on only countably many of them; countable choice makes the union over a countable functional family countable, leaving a nonzero quotient vector it misses.

items.title: Phillips' theorem, assuming countable choice: c-zero is not complemented in ell-infinity
items.strategy: Assume a bounded projection onto c-zero. Its complementary projection descends boundedly to ell-infinity/c-zero; composing with coordinate evaluations produces a countable separating family, contradicting the preceding lemma.

items.title: The closed uncomplemented subspace c-zero of ell-infinity
items.strategy: Package the closedness lemma and Phillips theorem as the requested concrete Banach-space example, retaining the countable-choice qualification rather than presenting it as an unconditional elementary argument.

items.title: Two different results are called Mazur's lemma
items.strategy: Name this page's weak-versus-norm closure theorem as Mazur's theorem, and distinguish it from the later convex-combination lemma for weakly convergent sequences.
